existing.description: The DAAD EPOS programme funds individual scholarships for graduates from developing and newly industrialised countries to take a development-oriented postgraduate (mostly Master's) course at a state or state-recognised German university, and in exceptional cases a doctoral degree. The award is a monthly payment of EUR 992 for graduates or EUR 1,300 for doctoral candidates (EUR 1,400 from February 2026), plus payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance and a flat-rate travel allowance. Under certain circumstances scholarship holders may additionally receive a monthly rent subsidy and a monthly allowance for accompanying family members. Scholarships are awarded subject to funding being provided by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).
eligibility: Graduates with at least two years' professional experience from the countries on the DAAD EPOS list of eligible countries
Bachelor degree (usually a four-year course) in an appropriate subject
Academic degree completed with far above average results (upper third)
At least two years of related professional experience after the first degree (bachelor) at the time of application
Academic degrees should normally not be more than six years old
Applicants who have been resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline cannot be considered

Working context is normally a public authority or a state or private company in a developing country, in planning and executing directives and projects with development-policy emphasis in technological, economic or social areas
Proof of development-related motivation and an expectation of taking on social responsibility and initiating and supporting processes of change after the scholarship
existing.eligibility_summary: Graduates with at least two years' professional experience from DAAD-listed developing and newly industrialised countries, who hold a relevant Bachelor degree with far above average results and whose degree is normally not more than six years old.
benefits: Monthly rent subsidy under certain circumstances
Monthly allowance for accompanying members of family under certain circumstances
Six-month preparatory German language course in Germany for scholarships for German-taught courses
coverage: Monthly scholarship payment of EUR 992 for graduates
Monthly scholarship payment of EUR 1,300 for doctoral candidates (EUR 1,400 beginning with February 2026)
Payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance cover
Travel allowance, unless these expenses are covered by the home country or another source of funding
requirements: Applications have only to be sent to the respective course directly; applications sent to the DAAD will not be forwarded to the course or university
You can apply for up to three courses; if applying for more than one course, list the courses in order of priority in the DAAD application forms and do not change the priorities
The complete applications have to be submitted in English or German to be considered
One uniform letter of motivation must be submitted to all postgraduate degree programmes of your choice, explaining the choice of courses and prioritisation
If the motivation letter does not explain the specific courses and priority order, the application cannot be considered or an already awarded scholarship may be withdrawn
Applicants from the People's Republic of China are asked to submit an APS Certificate with their application documents

For courses in German: a minimum German language level of B1 at the time of application, evidenced by a current certificate, and successful passing of DSH 2 or TestDaF 4 before the start of the study course
For courses in English: proof of adequate language skills according to the regulations of the respective course
Keep a copy of every document, because the documents must be uploaded as PDF files to the DAAD portal if you are suggested for a DAAD scholarship
documents: EPOS application form (Word document), typed or clearly legible
Curriculum vitae in reverse chronological order without unexplained gaps, using the europass template
One letter of motivation with detailed reference to academic, professional and personal reasons
Letter of recommendation from the current employer, on official letterhead, signed and stamped, of current date and not in a sealed envelope
Certificate(s) of employment showing at least two years of relevant work experience after the Bachelor's degree, ideally including a guarantee of re-employment upon returning home
Recent proof of language skills: English – IELTS or TOEFL (the institutional TOEFL is not accepted); German – required for courses taught in German
Copies of higher education degree certificates, with certified translation if not in German or English
Copy of the full set of transcript of records, with an explanation of the grading system if not part of the transcript
existing.english_requirement: English – IELTS or TOEFL (Note: the institutional TOEFL is not accepted). For courses taught in German, DSH 2 or TestDaF 4 must be passed before the course starts and a minimum German level of B1 must be proven at the time of application.
application_method: Step 1: Send your complete application directly to the postgraduate course you have chosen.
Step 2: A selection committee at the course suggests potential candidates for a DAAD scholarship.
Step 3: Suggested candidates are contacted by the DAAD and asked to upload their complete application to the DAAD portal.
Step 4: The selection process is finalised and the suggested candidates are informed accordingly.
existing.selection_notes: Selection is by independent, voluntary selection committees. Candidates must fulfil the academic requirements and be expected to complete the study programme successfully (above-average first academic exam, top performance in the third, language skills), hold a relevant Bachelor degree, have at least two years' professional experience, and prove a development-related motivation. Special circumstances such as a disability may be taken into account.
existing.best_fit: Graduates from DAC-listed developing and newly industrialised countries who hold a Bachelor (normally a four-year course) with above-average results (upper third), have at least two years of professional experience after that degree, and can prove a development-related motivation tied to their work in a public authority or company.
existing.notes: The scholarship call is made subject to the provision of funds by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), so funding is not guaranteed by the DAAD itself. Applications sent to the DAAD are not forwarded and will not be considered - the course must be applied to directly. Applicants resident in Germany for more than 15 months at the application deadline are excluded. Degrees should normally not be more than six years old. Some courses require additional documents. DAAD scholarships do not have to be paid back.
existing.application_period: Cycle-based: applicants apply directly to a listed EPOS postgraduate course for the published intake year (the current DAAD programme list is headed 'List of Application Deadlines for Intake 2027/2028'); the course's own committee then nominates candidates, who are invited to upload to the DAAD portal for the final selection.
existing.deadline_display: Depending on chosen study programme; please check the DAAD list of application deadlines or the website of the chosen study programme. Applications are sent directly to the course, not to the DAAD.

scholarships.title: Doctoral Scholarships — Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes (German Academic Scholarship Foundation)
scholarships.official_source: Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes (German Academic Scholarship Foundation)

existing.description: The Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes is Germany's largest scholarship foundation and funds around 350 new doctoral students each year with a monthly stipend of EUR 1,650 for three years. Since 2024 it has replaced regional application rounds with four fixed two-week calls a year, each opening about eight months before the selection meeting. Applications are accepted only by post and must be complete. The current call runs from 1 to 14 October 2026, with the selection meeting in May 2027 and the earliest possible scholarship start on 1 July 2027.
eligibility: German citizens, or foreign nationals who obtained their higher education entrance qualification in Germany, may apply
Doctoral study at a German university; enrolment is not mandatory but admission to a doctoral programme is required before funding starts

Doctoral thesis submitted at a university abroad is possible for German citizens and for foreign nationals who obtained their entrance qualification in Germany, subject to the availability of funds and to a justification of why the project belongs at the foreign university
Previous degree normally completed within the last four years and three months, with allowances for pregnancy, childcare, serious illness and care of close relatives
Expected to be among the top 15% of the year of graduation, judged across different disciplinary cultures
Applications cannot be submitted twice; a rejection in pre-selection or main selection is final
existing.eligibility_summary: Doctoral students who are German citizens or who obtained their higher education entrance qualification in Germany and are pursuing a doctorate at a German university; the previous degree must normally have been completed within the last four years and three months, and applicants are expected to be among the top 15% of their cohort.
benefits: Annual research allowance of up to EUR 100
Health insurance contribution up to EUR 100 per month
Family and childcare allowances, plus possible reallocation of funds from the final funding year
Separate travel grants for research visits and conferences abroad
Academic support including summer academies, research groups, language courses, workshops and supervision by liaison professors
coverage: Monthly stipend of EUR 1,650 for doctoral study in Germany
Research allowance of up to EUR 100 paid at the end of each year
Contribution of 50% of documented health insurance costs, up to EUR 100 per month, where insurance is not covered by employment
Additional grants towards research travel abroad, laboratory visits and conferences
requirements: Complete application pack submitted by post
Supervisor's questionnaire completed by the first reviewer
Scientifically demanding and innovative doctoral project
Evidence of individual study organisation and commitment to social causes
Signed declaration on security-relevant aspects of the research project
documents: Signed declaration on security-relevant aspects of the research project
Supervisor's questionnaire (an English version is available on the Studienstiftung website)
Degree certificates and transcripts supporting the ranking in the year of graduation
Documents evidencing individually organised studies and commitment to social causes
Project description for the doctoral studies
application_method: Post the complete application documents to Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes, Team Promotionsfoerderung, Ahrstr. 41, 53175 Bonn, Germany
Application forms and the supervisor questionnaire are supplied by the Studienstiftung; a second selection stage includes a personal interview at the foundation
existing.selection_notes: Two selection phases. Applicants are assessed on the academic standard of the previous degree, individual organisation of studies, commitment to social causes and the scientific quality of the doctoral project, which is reviewed in the second phase by two academically qualified reviewers. Scholars are not given bonus points, but statistically former scholarship holders are more likely to be funded. Involvement in security-relevant research requires a signed declaration before the procedure can proceed.
existing.best_fit: High-achieving doctoral candidates at German universities who obtained their university entrance qualification in Germany, or German citizens, with a research-intensive doctorate project and a record of social engagement.
existing.notes: Funding can only begin once doctoral study has started full-time. Part-time work is permitted up to 0.25 of a full-time position in research and teaching, or a maximum of five hours a week elsewhere. A doctoral scholarship from another institution may not be held at the same time, and holders must report any other scholarship offered to them. The foundation offers no institutional insurance cover, does not pay thesis printing costs, and applicants pay their own travel costs to the second-stage interview.
existing.duration: Three years, extendable by up to six months on application, and by up to 12 months on childbirth
existing.program_type: Foundation-funded doctoral scholarship for study and research in Germany
